content.text: As days shorten and temperatures fall, trees stop producing chlorophyll, the green pigment that drives photosynthesis, and it breaks down. The yellow and orange pigments that were already in the leaves then become visible, while some trees also make new red pigments.

Your last draft:

Your own feedback on it:
The draft is two sentences and factually sound, but it fails the "no jargon" criterion: "chlorophyll" and "photosynthesis" are technical terms, and "pigments" is also specialist vocabulary. Rewrite both sentences in plain language, for example: "As days get shorter and colder, trees stop making the green colouring in their leaves, so it fades away. The yellow and orange colours that were hidden underneath then show through, and some trees also make new red colouring." Keep it to two sentences.

Write the improved draft now.
